title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Funding Fee: Amount, Exemption, Remittance and Financing
content:
## The fee

The VA Home Loan Guaranty funding fee is the loan amount, excluding the fee itself, multiplied by the program's funding fee percentage and divided by one hundred, rounded to the cent. The percentage is the program's first-use percentage when the loan is the veteran's first use of the benefit, and the program's subsequent-use percentage otherwise.

## Placement of a purchase

A purchase is placed in the down-payment band whose minimum (inclusive) and maximum (exclusive) contain its down payment.

## Exemption

No fee is charged when the veteran is exempt on any of the program's funding fee exemption grounds as of the closing date.

## Remittance and financing

The lender remits the fee within the program's remittance period of days after closing, and a late remittance adds the program's late charge percentage. The fee may be financed into the loan.

## Condition and result

| Condition at closing | Fee charged |
|---|---|
| The veteran is exempt on any exemption ground as of the closing date | None |
| Not exempt; the loan is the veteran's first use | Loan amount multiplied by the first-use percentage, divided by one hundred, rounded to the cent |
| Not exempt; the loan is a subsequent use | Loan amount multiplied by the subsequent-use percentage, divided by one hundred, rounded to the cent |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: a purchase with a 7 percent down payment, which sits in the band from 5 (inclusive) to 10 (exclusive); a loan amount of 250,000.00 dollars excluding the fee; a first use; the band's first-use percentage taken as 1.5; the veteran not exempt.

The fee is 250,000.00 multiplied by 1.5 and divided by one hundred, that is 3,750.00 dollars. Had the veteran been exempt on any ground as of the closing date, no fee would be charged. Financing the fee adds it to the loan; the loan amount on which the fee is figured still excludes the fee itself.
